newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers to discuss Mid-East, U.S. trade laws.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to discuss Mid-East, U.S. trade laws.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers meet on Tuesday for talks ranging from the Middle East crisis to retaliation against U.S. trade sanctions.
Ministers were gathering after Monday's meeting between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and the EU's so-called troika.

Arafat met the troika -- past, current and future presidents of the 15-nation bloc -- to thank them for continued support and brief them ahead of the Middle East summit in Washington later on Tuesday.

The EU, the biggest financial backer of the Palestinian authority, has been miffed at being excluded from the Washington summit, which will bring together Arafat, U.S. President Bill Clinton, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein.
The foreign ministers are expected to come out with a strong statement in support of peace after all 15 are briefed by the troika members, currently Italy, Ireland and the Netherlands.
They are also expected to discuss proposed retaliation to a rash of trade laws coming from Washington.

Although the European Commission -- the EU's executive -- is finalising counter measures to the Helms-Burton Act and the D'Amato Bill, the ministers are not expected to make a final decision on Tuesday.
Those laws, passed earlier this year to a chorus of indignation from some of Washington's strongest trade allies, seek to outlaw trade with Cuba, Iran and Libya.
Ministers are also expected to discuss British proposals for putting pressure on the military government of Burma following a clampdown on the fledgling democracy movement there.
They will also discuss elections in Bosnia as well as progress on the inter-governmental conference -- the ongoing reworking of the EU's treaties and agreements.
